new_agent_audits.name: new_debug_unreachable
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and the complete src/lib.rs, including both macro arms. The no_std macro expands to unreachable! in debug and to core::hint::unreachable_unchecked in release; it does not insert an unsafe block around that call, so release-capable callers must already provide unsafe context and prove the branch unreachable. Reaching it in release is undefined behavior: untrusted parse failures must use ordinary errors, never this optimization. The hidden reexport preserves the same unsafe API. The zero-argument recursive invocation is not fully hygienic and may fail if renamed/shadowed; this is a compile-time limitation, not input execution. No dependencies, build script, native payload, allocation or OS authority. This certifies the documented unsafe primitive, not the correctness of downstream unreachability proofs.

new_agent_audits.name: stable_deref_trait
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and all of src/lib.rs, including the complete unsafe trait contracts and every implementation. StableDeref requires stable storage across moves/shared operations; CloneStableDeref additionally preserves the same target across clones and must not be combined with mutable dereferencing. Box/Vec/String/CString/OsString/PathBuf own out-of-line storage; the listed Cow variants preserve borrowed or owned backing storage across shared methods. Rc/Arc clones share their allocation and Arc is gated on pointer atomics. References, Ref/RefMut and lock guards preserve the borrowed target for their lifetime; exclusive operations on the owning container are outside the contract. No blanket implementation for arbitrary user Deref types or runtime pointer manipulation is introduced. No dependencies, build script, native payload or OS calls; Path/lock types here are marker implementations, not file or synchronization operations. Incorrect downstream unsafe implementations and aliasing in consuming libraries require separate review.

new_agent_audits.name: dtoa-short
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and the complete src/lib.rs, including rounding, sign handling, exponent movement and both unsafe operations. Also inspected the locked dtoa 1.0.11 Buffer/Float API in src/lib.rs (separately covered dependency): Float is sealed to f32/f64 and Buffer owns 25 bytes; format_finite returns bounded ASCII even for nonfinite inputs, whose numeric value is unspecified. The scratch array has size_of(Buffer)+1 bytes and is separate from the source, so copying the returned bytes starting at offset one fits without overlap. Precision is the internal constant 6 or 15, never caller-controlled. Rounding and forward exponent compaction stay within the initialized slice and preserve ASCII; the unchecked UTF-8 conversion therefore receives valid bytes. Zero/sign/large-exponent paths use checked slicing; custom fmt::Write remains caller code. Output is deliberately lossy and nonfinite values are not faithfully represented: unsuitable for exact numeric protocols, monetary calculations or authentication encodings. No allocation, build script, native payload or OS authority. Dependency internals are not recertified by the supporting API inspection.

new_agent_audits.name: find_cuda_helper
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)

new_agent_audits.name: async-recursion
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and all three production modules (lib.rs, parse.rs, expand.rs). Arguments accept only optional ?Send and Sync, rejecting duplicates, excess and other syntax; the item must be an async function. Expansion removes async from the signature, adds explicit generic/reference outlives bounds and returns Pin<Box<dyn Future>> around Box::pin(async move { original body }). It adds Send/Sync bounds, never unsafe implementations or lifetime casts, so the Rust type checker enforces transfer/borrow validity. Newly synthesized lifetime names and the unqualified Box can collide with caller names; unsupported typed-self or nested-reference cases can reject otherwise valid source rather than bypass the type checker. The original function body and its authority remain caller code. Runtime recursion depth, allocation and exponential algorithms are not bounded by this transformation. No unsafe code, environment/file/network/process operations, build script or native payload. Reviewed generated deployed behavior, not just macro-host behavior.

new_agent_audits.name: enumflags2_derive
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and the complete generator, and cross-read the RawBitFlags contract and consumers in enumflags2 0.7.12. Accepts only non-generic, unit-variant enums with fixed unsigned u8/u16/u32/u64/u128 representation; signed/usize/other representations are rejected and rustc checks layout, discriminant range and uniqueness. Literal and shift folding uses checked shifts; explicit flags must be powers of two, deferred expressions get compile-time power-of-two assertions, and inferred values select an unused bit. Too many variants are rejected. The generated unsafe RawBitFlags implementation uses that same representation, casts real enum values, ORs real variants for ALL_BITS/default and emits no transmute itself; these properties justify the runtime single-bit transmute consumers. Malformed attributes, cfg variants or overflowing inferred constants may fail compilation. Caller expressions/attributes remain trusted Rust source, not data to sandbox. No file/env/process/network access, build script or native payload.

new_agent_audits.name: enumflags2
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and all five production modules, including serde, const API and every macro expansion. Cross-read the matching derive generator. Safe constructors mask or reject bits outside ALL_BITS; union/intersection/xor/not preserve that invariant. Manual RawBitFlags implementations and unchecked constructors are explicitly unsafe caller contracts. No build script, native payload, dynamic allocation for flag operations or OS authority. Malicious unsafe impls and arbitrary caller trait implementations are outside this audit.

new_agent_audits.name: rustc-hash
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and all three modules, including optional rand/nightly branches and unit tests. All production operations are safe Rust. Byte hashing handles empty and short lengths before indexing, consumes fixed 16-byte chunks and uses a proven in-bounds suffix for longer inputs. Integer mixing is explicitly wrapping with fixed shifts/rotations and separate 32/64-bit paths. Seeded builders return independent scalar hash state; optional randomness uses a thread-local Cell initialized through rand and wrapping increments, without direct OS calls here. FxHashMap/FxHashSet are standard containers with this hasher. This is explicitly noncryptographic and not HashDoS-resistant, including with the random seed option; attacker-controlled large key sets need application resource bounds or a different hasher. It must not be used for authentication, secret fingerprints or anonymity. No unsafe, build script, packaged native code, file/process/network access or logging. Optional dependency behavior is separate.

new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)

new_agent_audits.name: phf
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and all five production modules, including both CHD/ptrhash layouts, cfg trampolines, iterator implementations and optional serde serialization. new_agent_audits.name: markup5ever
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and all six production modules. Inspected the single unsafe block in BufferQueue::pop_except_from: the prefix scanner stops only on ASCII below 64, so its byte count is either the whole valid UTF-8 tendril or a character boundary; count never exceeds the tendril's u32 length. The shared subtendril retains backing ownership before the original prefix is removed, satisfying the tendril API contracts. Queue operations use RefCell and checked containers; reentrant callbacks, self-swap, emptied mutable front chunks or a comparator that splits UTF-8 can panic rather than cause unchecked reads. SmallCharSet membership shifts only after the less-than-64 guard. Generic standalone strings larger than u32 can overflow the prefix count; it is not a general unbounded-string API. TreeSink/Serializer are caller interfaces: helpers only compute namespace/template/integration flags and forward data, including explicit duplicate-attribute information. Script/encoding markers do not execute content. Debug/errors can expose names/content; consumers must control logging and escaping. No build.rs, native payload or OS authority. Dependencies and actual parsers/serializers need separate audits.

new_agent_audits.name: memoffset
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests, build.rs and all four production modules, including all historical cfg branches and tests. On NymWrap's pinned Rust 1.100 the fixed version probes enable MaybeUninit, addr_of, stable_const and stable_offset_of: ordinary/tuple/union offsets use core::mem::offset_of!, and span computation uses raw field addresses in a live MaybeUninit allocation. Field-pattern checks prevent implicit Deref traversal; caller expressions are evaluated outside inserted unsafe blocks. Offsets/spans are layout information only, not reads of padding or uninitialized contents. raw_field helpers require a live non-dangling correctly typed base pointer; they do not validate arbitrary pointers. Historical pre-MaybeUninit/pre-addr_of fallbacks explicitly contain known unsound constructions and are not accepted as a portable soundness claim: discretion is limited to this project's enforced modern compiler; do not reuse this review to support old compilers. Span ordering/padding for repr(Rust) is not a stable serialization contract. Build authority is limited to autocfg compiler probes and fixed cfg stdout; no own file/network/process calls or native payload. No assurance for caller unsafe use or separately reviewed autocfg.

new_agent_audits.name: derive_more
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests and all ten production modules, including every feature-gated helper and reexport. new_agent_audits.name: constant_time_eq
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests, build.rs and all five source modules, including generic/SSE2/AVX/NEON paths and ARM DIT detection/guards. Unsafe word/vector loads receive checked exact-size slices after equal-length checks, use unaligned-capable operations and read only initialized byte/integer/vector types. Each loop consumes 16/32 bytes or one Word; tails use successively bounded integer widths, preserving a difference accumulator without data-dependent early exits. Register-only comparison/mask assembly declares inputs/outputs and does not touch memory or stack; SIMD modules are gated on corresponding target features. The atomic ARM feature cache is private and stores only valid Features discriminants; relaxed ordering suffices because it publishes no separate data. DIT/SB instructions follow standard feature detection or explicit unsafe caller overrides, and guards restore the saved DIT value on unwind. Build output is fixed cfg data selected from compiler version/target environment. Length and address timing remains observable; no universal hardware/compiler side-channel proof, instruction-count measurement, ARM execution or formal cryptographic audit is claimed. No native payload, dynamic allocation, file/network/process API or content logging. Tests cover functional equality and boundaries separately.

new_agent_audits.name: xdg-home
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests, README and the complete single module, including Unix/Windows FFI and its test. HOME is accepted verbatim, including empty/relative paths; it is trusted local configuration, not validated storage policy. The Unix fallback calls geteuid/getpwuid_r with a live passwd output and 1024-byte scratch buffer, checks return code/result/pw_dir before CStr conversion, and copies the returned directory before stack storage expires. Insufficient buffer space returns None without examining uninitialized output. Windows passes the Profile GUID and null user token, reads the successful API-owned NUL-terminated UTF-16 path, copies it and frees it with CoTaskMemFree. Primary Linux man-pages and Microsoft SHGetKnownFolderPath contracts were checked. Explicit discretion: failure or invalid UTF-16 paths can leak an OS allocation because early returns miss freeing; this is a local-profile resource leak, not certified as leak-free. No shell, file writes or direct network API; OS user-database/NSS lookup may itself perform OS-configured I/O, so sandbox restrictions still apply. Returned paths are sensitive and must not bypass NymWrap storage/encryption policy or be sent remotely. No build script or packaged native code.

new_agent_audits.name: ordered-stream
new_agent_audits.who: NymWrap source review (Codex agent; not human)
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests, README, the complete OrderedStream/OrderedFuture contracts and all executable code in all four source modules (large rustdoc example blocks omitted from the implementation view; no claim to have read those examples in full). Pin projections keep child streams/futures pinned; explicit Unpin implementations wrap pinned references or require Unpin children before constructing pins. Buffered items are ordinary owned values; Then replaces/drops completed pinned futures through pin-project-lite rather than moving them. Join polls each side with bounded retries; multi-join performs at most two finite passes over caller collections, with one buffered item per stream. Size-hint sums use saturating/checked arithmetic. Filter/filter_map can consume an unbounded always-ready rejected stream in one poll, so callers need bounded/cooperative sources; no fairness guarantee is claimed. Found a logic limitation in Join::position_hint's B-buffered arm: it consults stream_b instead of stream_a, so hints can overestimate the minimum of future items. Do not use hints or source ordering as an authorization/replay boundary; validate protocol order separately. Ordering mappers, comparisons, callbacks and child polling remain caller code. No own unsafe blocks, build script, native payload, OS authority or text execution. Pin-project-lite and other dependencies require separate coverage.
